records.description: Tidal River Avon at Bristol, Pill and Shirehampton
records.message:
Higher than normal tides over the next two days may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from early evening on Monday and on Tuesday morning. 
Areas most at risk include the tidal River Avon from Sea Mills to Conham in Bristol and between the Avonmouth Bridge and Shirehampton Park including Pill and Shirehampton. 
The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Avonmouth of 7.50 mAODN at 7:00 PM on Monday 26/10/2026, which is 0.55 m above tide tables, with southerly force 5 winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.)			
The second forecast high water is at 7:30 AM on Tuesday 27/10/2026 with a level of 7.37 mAODN which is 0.38 m above tide tables, with south westerly force 6 winds. 
We are closely monitoring the situation and will issue further Alerts or updates as necessary. 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 1:00PM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.

records.description: Severn estuary from Gloucester to Sharpness
records.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 8am to 10am on 27/10/2026. 
Tidal flooding may affect low lying land and roads adjacent to the Estuary from Sandhurst to Chepstow and Sharpness over the next 3 days. Some lengths of the flood embankment at Longney and The Noards may be overtopped. Rodley Lane, Westbury and Awre Road, Brims Pill may be flooded. Predicted peaks: Sandhurst 3.3m to 3.5mm on 27/10 09:45AM, Gloucester 3.3m to 3.5m on 27/10 09:30AM. Sandhurst 3.3m to 3.6m on 27/10 22:00PM, Gloucester 3.3m to 3.5m on 27/10 22:00PM. Tidal peak impacts are not forecast to affect other gauging points. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads and low lying roads near rivers, which may be flooded.   
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.

There is no longer a threat of flooding.
We do not expect to see similar impacts from the next high tide. Although tide levels will remain high until Thursday, wind conditions are improving and there is reduced risk as a result.
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.
